checks: The proper barycentric section has centroid a_i at i and (1−a_i)/d in all other positions. Subtracting a gives zero i-coordinate, zero coordinate sum and delta_i·a=−||delta_i||².

Differentiate the exact corner-simplex volume in a_i to obtain the coarea S_i. The chosen margin velocity integrates to −S_i||delta_i||² at a fixed mark, and the centroid-zero condition at two indices forces the canonical vector for d≥2.
In both definitions of h and k, the sum of h is zero and h_i+k_i||delta_i||²=1. The initially proper cut therefore has derivative −S_i<0 under the combined cap and mark motion.
The perturbed margin vector is U_epsilon(λ−a(epsilon)). Its weighted sum is identically zero with positive weights U_epsilon^{-T}1 for small epsilon, preserving actual whole-affine-span coverage.

For canonical thresholds, some cap in any full cover contains the centroid and pays at least Γ_d V. The one-high mark is the centroid of the ratio-1/3 corner copy; its high cap exactly meets the lower bound Γ_d V/3^d and cannot decrease at that fixed mark.
Checked the explicit low-section displacement coordinates and squared norm, as well as the d=1 exchange of the two interval lengths. The source §§3–4 supports all of these scopes.

dependencies.hypotheses: The proper single-simplex sections obey its two-sided first variation, by using a single integer dummy base if desired. The nonlinear path has the displayed linear velocity and its O(t²) margin difference gives only o(t) volume by slicing.
Move any containing halfspace boundary to the simplex centroid, apply the Γ_q bound with q≤d, and use monotonicity of Γ_q. Apply the same bound to the ratio-1/3 simplex centered at the high mark.

overlap.comparison: It covers the centroid lower bounds used for canonical and one-high calibration, but says nothing about the explicit descent of all noncanonical concurrent caps.

It constructs the same one-high patterns at the endpoint of an actual mixed star and freezes all cap parameters during a body motion. The present descent concerns an ordinary fixed simplex and moving cap parameters.
